expo-milnor-clarity.evidence: H5: circular — L1 defines the weight subcategory as sums of 'the weight spaces of $V$', and then defines $T$ as the subgroup acting diagonally on those weight spaces; weight spaces presuppose a torus. Weight spaces of $\tau(V)$ are subspaces of a module, not objects of $\mathbf C$. H6: the tikz square (L7-16) does not encode the definition. H2: no picture first ($\mathrm{diag}(e^{i\theta},e^{-i\theta})$).
expo-milnor-clarity.notes: Milnor H1-H8 = [2, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1] (T=8/16, fail); weakest: H2, H3, H4, H5, H6, H7, H8. Suggested rewrite (not applied; owner rule 'ask before changing'): Define via a chosen decomposition: 'Fix a decomposition $\tau(V)=L_+\oplus L_-$ into rank-one summands. The maximal torus $T\subseteq G$ is the subgroup preserving each $L_\pm$; for $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, $T=\{\mathrm{diag}(e^{i\theta},e^{-i\theta})\}$.' Drop the tikz square. Audit doc: docs/audits/2026-10-10-milnor-voice-audit-ch1-ch2.md

trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Full read: definition block with a tikzcd diagram. Register clean: three declaratives plus an 'Equivalently, ...' restatement, which is a standard mathematical equivalent-characterisation sentence rather than category-7 thesis restatement (it states a different, non-obvious characterisation: T is the largest subgroup under which every object of <V> splits into lines). No dash, no triple, no closer, no announced emphasis, no superlative used for emphasis ('largest subgroup' is a precise extremal claim).
trap-negation-contrast.notes: No trap. Two structural flags, neither fixed: (1) the displayed T = Aut^(x)(tau|_<V>) is asserted as a SUBgroup of G, but restricting a fibre functor to a full subcategory yields a group receiving a homomorphism FROM G (a quotient in the Tannakian dictionary); the block's own diagram draws T hook-> G from the different 'acts diagonally' characterisation. I could not adjudicate whether the two coincide for this particular <V>. (2) lean.ref qou:QOU.MaximalTorus resolves to nothing, and a definition block requires a Lean sibling. Both in the returned anomaly list.
